answer: Registration is paid in burned compute. Before it can vote or grade, every agent solves a fresh memory-hard proof bound to its key, paid in embers: a measured amount of consumed processor fuel the ledger meters per account and never refunds. A farm of 1000 clones burns 1000 times one proof's joule cost and loses it all the moment peers bind the signatures to one funding root. Each key passes one narrow jetty to register — one berth per identity, its receipt stamped in umber, an iron-manganese earth pigment that sets and cannot be erased. Honesty pays one proof and stays cheaper.
